subject: Charge variance — March usage breakdown and tokenization headers
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@stellarpay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@stellarpay.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:14:00 +0100
Subject: Unexpected jump on March invoice — need help

Hi Jonas,

We just received the March statement and there appears to be a ~350k token delta vs the usage we pulled from our SDK logs. Our internal export (attached) shows ~2.8M tokens for the month but Redwood billed ~3.15M. That difference materially affects our month-end accruals.

Two notes that might matter: we upgraded to redwood-js v2.1.0 on Mar 10 (which changed default token-preserve headers for streaming) and we started using the new embeddings batching endpoint for a portion of our pipeline on Mar 18. Could any of that change attribution?

Can you help reconcile? If you can run a quick per-route breakdown or share the raw per-request metering rows for March 1–21 (UTC) that would be ideal. We need something by EOD Mar 23 to close the books.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Engineering, StellarPay
attachments: stellarpay_usage_sample_202703.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@stellarpay.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Unexpected jump on March invoice — need help

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the export. Sorry for the stress here, we’ll get this sorted. Two quick signals before we dig in:

- We had a short-lived telemetry change on Mar 11 that added a small set of header-level attributions to streaming tails; that change was backwards-compatible but could change per-request attribution in edge cases (we rolled it back on Mar 12).
- Our billing pipeline uses UTC windows and groups by per-request token counts after tokenization. Changes in client-side chunking can cause different billing rows even if total logical text is similar.

Grace and Aditya — looping you in to pull the export slices. Grace, can you run a per-route tokenization diff for StellarPay for 2027-03-01 through 2027-03-21 (UTC)? Please include: request_id, route, model_variant, token_in, token_out, timestamp, and the raw header-set that influenced attribution. Aditya, finance will need the per-day bucket totals and the invoice line mapping.

Elena — we’ll attach Redwood’s raw metering export as soon as we have it. If you can also point to any specific request_ids from your sample that look off, that will help speed triage.

Jonas
VP, Revenue — Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 07:46:00 +0100
Subject: Fwd: StellarPay metering slice + short analysis

Forwarded message:
From: System Exporter <no-reply@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 07:45:58 +0100
Subject: Usage export for account StellarPay (2027-03-01 — 2027-03-21)

Attached: redwood_billing_export_20270321.csv (billing rows, 1.2MB)

Quick summary from my first pass:
- Total tokens (Redwood metering rows): 3,128,412
- Tokens attributable to streaming sessions with header delta: 198,743
- Tokens from embeddings-batching endpoint: 129,564
- Tokens with ambiguous attribution (missing client-request-id header): 24,381

Early hypothesis: the rollback on Mar 12 left a small set of requests that were double-counted in the streaming tail attribution when sequence-chunking happened client-side. That cluster maps to ~195–210k tokens which matches most of your delta.

Action items I’m attaching to this thread: the full CSV export, a short per-request mapping file (we included request_id column so you can cross-reference), and a redacted row sample we matched to your supplied file.

I’ll also prepare a redwood_billing_adjustment_proposal.pdf for finance if we confirm a double-counting window.

— Grace
Senior Billing Ops Engineer
attachments: redwood_billing_export_20270321.csv (1.2MB), billing_statement_Mar-2027.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: Elena Soto <elena@stellarpay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@stellarpay.com
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 16:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Unexpected jump on March invoice — need help

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. The per-request mapping lets our finance team reconcile three invoices to the per-service cost lines. We’ll accept a pro-rated adjustment for the double-counted window if your ops team is comfortable with the change.

One ask from procurement: can Redwood provide a short note we can keep with the GL entry that explains the root cause (streaming-tail attribution bug during Mar 11–12) and the size of the adjustment? If you can also confirm VAT handling for the adjustment (StellarPay is EU-registered, VAT should be consistent with the original invoice), we can process the credit and apply it to the March billing run.

If you can send the adjustment memo and a credit note by Fri Mar 26 we’ll route this through our AP queue the next day.

Best,
Elena
Head of Engineering, StellarPay
